references.source:
Binoy Koshy\.
A sociolinguistic study of bagheli speakers in madhya pradesh\.
Technical Report 2022\-015, SIL International, 2022\.
The report was created in 2004 and published in 2022\. All eighteen target lects attach to canonical Bagheli\. Similarity\-group numbers remain source notes and are not treated as historical cognacy\. Two readable forms lacking any printed site code remain excluded, one source\-questioned form is installed without punctuation but explicitly annotated, and one uppercase site code is interpreted conservatively at medium confidence\. The report names localities but supplies no defensible historical collection coordinates\.
URL: [https://www\.sil\.org/resources/archives/94596](https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/94596)\.
references.progress: Appendix B.4, printed pages 50--72: 5,828 manually transcribed Bagheli source-local occurrence rows from eighteen locality lists, yielding 5,829 compiled lexical variants after the source's comma-separated alternatives at item 173 site m are expanded. Two hundred eighty-three Standard Hindi occurrences, twenty-four non-lexical by-name occurrences, forty-seven blank conceptual cells, and two legible but site-unassigned response lines are audit-only
references.provenance: Official SIL publisher PDF downloaded 2026-08-28, SHA-256 d1424f317dc12fe01d99d33abd917201575487f4de44529678ecce1c282a4627; the PDF is not redistributed. Reproducible embedded-image extraction, 92-column OCR comparison scaffold, frozen manual transcription, source-local importer, complete 6,184-record audit and manifest are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_bagheli_2022; installed rows are data/other/forms/20260828-sil-bagheli.csv

The malvi\-speaking people of madhya pradesh and rajasthan: a sociolinguistic profile\.

The report states that schwa, turned a, turned v and alpha are used interchangeably and assumes no phonemic distinction among them\. Source IPA remains in Original/Phonemic while a dedicated display profile applies Jambu conventions\. Lexical\-similarity category numbers and letters are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Thirty\-four used legacy CIDs were resolved without OCR: thirty\-one from the report's own IPA chart and three from the official SAG\-IPA conversion table plus rendered\-page checks\. The Thillorkhurd extraction was independently compared to its later Unicode reprint in ESR 2012\-002, with 132 exact response matches across 126 concepts\. Printed source metadata provide localities and administrative units but no point coordinates, so the thirty dialect rows intentionally leave coordinates blank\.

references.source:
Jeff Webster\.
Sociolinguistic survey of haryanvi\.
Technical Report 2024\-011, SIL International, 2024\.
The survey was conducted from August to October 1991\. Section 4\.1\.1 explicitly defines the printed group numbers as phonological\-similarity judgments rather than cognate relationships; Jambu retains them only as source notes\. Seven same\-list cross\-references are resolved deterministically\. Typed audit notes preserve faint, unlabelled and clipped fragments without guessing them into installed forms\. The report names the six localities but gives no point coordinates, so dialect coordinates remain blank\.
URL: [https://www\.sil\.org/system/files/reapdata/39/32/25/39322561837182664281680018892812535354/JLSR2024\\\_011\.pdf](https://www.sil.org/system/files/reapdata/39/32/25/39322561837182664281680018892812535354/JLSR2024\_011.pdf)\.
references.progress: Appendix A.3, printed pages 21--34: 1,553 manually transcribed lexical variants from all 1,238 responsive cells in the six HRT, HJN, HFT, HNG, HTR and HLH Haryanvi lists. Twenty-one visibly blank target cells and one elicitation-only target cell are audit-only. The 840 BPL Braj/Haryanvi, PBG Baghati Pahari, HIN Hindustani and PUN Punjabi comparison cells are retained audit-only and are not manually transcribed

Brad Chamberlain and Wendy Chamberlain\.
A sociolinguistic survey of lahul valley, himachal pradesh\.
Technical Report 2019\-006, SIL International, 8 2019\.
The report explicitly says that the field transcriptions have not undergone thorough phonological analysis\. Similarity\-group labels are retained as source notes and do not assert historical cognacy\. Modern quality\-C locality points are used because the report supplies regional maps but no point coordinates\.
